title: La Grande Bretèche (1)
author: Honoré de Balzac
note: Late at night, after a dinner party in Paris, the famous doctor Bianchon tells a true story from his youth: an abandoned house near Vendôme, in the Loire valley, and the secret behind it. The story uses the passé simple, a literary past tense: when you hear je vis, il dit, or elle mourut, just think: I saw, he said, she died.

segments.fr: — Monsieur, lui dis-je en terminant,
segments.en: "Monsieur," I said to him in conclusion,

segments.fr: vous m'avez si vivement impressionné,
segments.en: "you have made such a vivid impression on me

segments.fr: que je crois voir cette mourante plus pâle que ses draps ;

segments.fr: ses yeux luisants me font peur,
segments.en: her gleaming eyes frighten me,

segments.fr: et je rêverai d'elle cette nuit.
segments.en: and I shall dream of her tonight.

segments.en: But you must have formed some guesses

segments.fr: — Monsieur, me dit-il avec une réserve comique,
segments.en: "Monsieur," he said to me with comical reserve,

segments.fr: je ne me permets jamais de juger la conduite des personnes
